name: Group3r - GPO Misconfiguration Analysis
description: Analyzes Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to find misconfigurations and security weaknesses: writable GPO links, script paths with weak permissions, insecure scheduled tasks, credential exposure in GPP, and SYSVOL write access. Outputs a log of findings ranked by severity.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHAT GROUP3R CHECKS ===
Group3r audits every GPO visible to the current user and flags:
  - GPO links the current user can write/modify
  - Script paths in GPO startup/logon scripts with weak ACLs (hijackable)
  - Scheduled tasks inside GPOs calling writable scripts or binaries
  - Plaintext passwords in GPP (though mostly patched, older DCs may still have them)
  - SYSVOL and NETLOGON share write permissions

=== USAGE ===
  -f <log>      Write output to file (recommended - output is verbose)
  -s <server>   Target DC (default: auto-detect from domain)
  -u <user>     User for auth (default: current session)
  Run as a domain user - no special privileges needed for read access.

=== WORKFLOW ===
1. Run group3r.exe -f group3r.log
2. Review log for 'HIGH' and 'CRITICAL' severity items
3. GPO write access → use ad-gpo-enum / PowerView to confirm scope
4. Writable script paths → plant a payload to catch next GPO refresh
5. Credential findings → try with crackmapexec / evil-winrm

=== COMPARED TO OTHER GPO TOOLS ===
  PowerView Get-GPO/Get-GPOReport: raw enumeration, manual analysis needed
  SharpGPOAbuse: exploitation (not just enumeration)
  Group3r: automated misconfiguration hunting with severity ranking

examples.label: Run and write findings to log

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

recommended.note: Enumerate GPOs with PowerView first to understand scope, then use Group3r for automated misconfiguration analysis.
After Group3r finds writable SYSVOL/NETLOGON paths, Snaffler can hunt credentials in accessible files.

defense.why_it_works: Group3r reads GPO definitions and evaluates file system ACLs on referenced paths. Any authenticated domain user can read GPOs via SYSVOL - the misconfiguration is the weak ACLs, not the read access itself.
defense.prerequisites: Domain-joined Windows host; authenticated domain user session.
defense.impact: Identifies exploitable GPO paths enabling code execution on every machine in the GPO scope, potential DA via scheduled task or startup script hijacking.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1484.001 M1018] Restrict GPO write access to dedicated admin accounts; audit SYSVOL and NETLOGON share ACLs regularly; use Microsoft's Group Policy Modeling to review effective policy before deployment.
defense.misconfiguration: IT teams often grant broad write access to SYSVOL or to individual GPO objects for operational convenience. Script paths in GPO startup/logon tasks may point to shares with weak permissions, allowing any domain user to replace the script.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# GPO Startup Script points to a world-writable share:
# GPO: \\inlanefreight.local\SYSVOL\...\scripts\startup.bat
icacls \\inlanefreight.local\SYSVOL\...\scripts\startup.bat
# Output: Everyone:(F) - full control for all users
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict script path ACLs - only SYSTEM and Domain Admins
icacls \\inlanefreight.local\SYSVOL\...\scripts /inheritance:r /grant 'Domain Admins:(OI)(CI)F' SYSTEM:F
# Audit GPO delegations quarterly:
Get-GPPermission -All -DomainName inlanefreight.local | Where-Object { $_.Permission -eq 'GpoEdit' }
defense.evasion: Read the exposed data with least interaction; revert any change you make; scope queries narrowly to avoid bulk-read alerts.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 Image="*Group3r*"
| table _time, Computer, User, CommandLine

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5145 Share_Name="*SYSVOL*"
| table _time, Computer, Account_Name, Relative_Target_Name
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.name:*Group3r* OR (event.code:"5145" AND winlog.event_data.ShareName:*SYSVOL*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has "Group3r"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| union (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 5145 and ShareName has "SYSVOL" | project Timestamp=TimeGenerated, DeviceName=Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, ProcessCommandLine=RelativeTargetName)
| sort by Timestamp desc
// Group3r reads GPOs from SYSVOL looking for misconfigurations

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Sysmon, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Audits GPOs for misconfigurations and secrets:
  group3r.exe   walk every GPO the current user can read
  -f <output_log>   write findings to this log file
Flags writable GPO links, weak script paths, insecure scheduled tasks, and credentials in GPP; run as a domain user and grep the log for HIGH/CRITICAL, or -s to target a specific DC.
